formulations.definition: A discrete-time real-valued martingale (X_n,F_n)_{n≥0} is an adapted process with E|X_n|<∞ for every n and E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=X_n almost surely for each n≥0.
Equivalently, an adapted integrable discrete-time process is a martingale if E[X_m|F_n]=X_n almost surely for every pair of indices 0≤n≤m.

proposed_contextual_meanings.context: continuous-time martingale indexed by nonnegative real times

formulations.definition: A continuous-time martingale (X_t,F_t)_{t≥0} is an adapted process with E|X_t|<∞ for every t and E[X_t|F_s]=X_s almost surely whenever 0≤s≤t.

mathematical_review: ProofWiki distinguishes discrete-time one-step from all-later-time forms and separately treats continuous time. The one-step and all-later-time discrete conditions are equivalent by the tower property of conditional expectation, provided integrability and adaptedness hold. Almost-sure equality is essential. Continuous-time martingale does NOT by itself assert almost surely continuous sample paths; the word continuous here refers to the time index. These contexts should be separately displayed under a common term, not conflated with local martingales, supermartingales or deterministic processes.

term: chromatic number of a finite simple graph

proposed_contextual_meanings.context: finite simple undirected graph with nonempty vertex set

formulations.definition: For a finite simple undirected graph G with at least one vertex, its chromatic number χ(G) is the least positive integer k for which there exists a map c:V(G)→{1,…,k} satisfying c(u)≠c(v) for every edge {u,v}.

Equivalently, for a finite simple graph G with at least one vertex, χ(G) is the least positive integer k such that P_G(k)>0, where P_G(k) counts proper vertex colorings using a fixed palette of k labeled colors.

mathematical_review: MathWorld gives minimum proper vertex colors and the equivalent first positive value of the chromatic polynomial. Both formulations are for vertex, not edge or total, coloring. A k-coloring may use fewer than k different colors. The nonempty-vertex finite simple-graph restriction avoids disagreements over the chromatic number of the graph with zero vertices, and loops are excluded because a looped graph cannot have a proper vertex coloring. A new MathWorld source record needs its own rights/access review and locator-only policy before pipeline ingestion.
